item.text: The importer uses YAML v2 today, which produces `map[interface{}]interface{}` for nested values. I’m checking the document decoder and namespace model now; the fix needs to switch only YAML decoding to v3 while keeping JSON’s standard decoder and its narrowly scoped first-line comment handling.

index 12d4fbc..14f449e 100644
--- a/internal/ext/encoding.go
+++ b/internal/ext/encoding.go
@@ -1,10 +1,11 @@
 package ext
 
 import (
+	"bufio"
 	"encoding/json"
 	"io"
 
-	"gopkg.in/yaml.v2"
+	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
 )
 
 type Encoding string
@@ -46,12 +47,23 @@ func (e Encoding) NewDecoder(r io.Reader) Decoder {
 	case EncodingYML, EncodingYAML:
 		return yaml.NewDecoder(r)
 	case EncodingJSON:
-		return json.NewDecoder(r)
+		return json.NewDecoder(stripJSONHeader(r))
 	}
 
 	return nil
 }
 
+// stripJSONHeader ignores a single leading comment line used by JSON exports.
+// JSON itself does not support comments, so leave all other content untouched.
+func stripJSONHeader(r io.Reader) io.Reader {
+	br := bufio.NewReader(r)
+	line, err := br.Peek(1)
+	if err == nil && len(line) == 1 && line[0] == '#' {
+		_, _ = br.ReadString('\n')
+	}
+	return br
+}
+
 type Decoder interface {
 	Decode(any) error
 }

item.text:
Updated [encoding.go](/app/internal/ext/encoding.go) to use the YAML v3 decoder and ignore one leading `#` line for JSON imports. This lets nested metadata decode into JSON compatible maps and arrays while leaving ordinary YAML and JSON decoding intact.

Verification: `go test ./internal/ext` passed.
